text_fidelity_a:
Tile - (Gen 1) - 1 Pack - Discontinued by Manufacturer The Tile system isn't perfect but it works (mostly) and to date I haven't run across any better options. So bearing in mind your needs and the device's limitations, it's probably worth getting (at the time of this writing) if you have things you're worried about misplacing.

Pros:

- EASY setup. The time it takes to send an eMail and receive a reply, and a few seconds more. I have heard people say it requires iPhone 4 and up - I have a 5 and everything was a breeze. I didn't use the picture feature initially but it was no problem to update later.

- Decent map feature - good enough to get you in general range of the FIND radius.

- An audible FIND jingle. Just loud enough to hear through a wallet. Louder sure would be better, but it has a tinny high-pitched jingle that's easy to identify once you've heard it.

- It's small enough to fit in my wallet. It's a bit bulky, but it does.

- It's weatherproof and sealed. I haven't actually tested that and don't want to, but it's a nice feature.

- On-phone settings are easy to operate, and allow you to turn off Bluetooth tracking without turning off the iPhone's Bluetooth.

- Easy to assign to other objects as needed (if you don't use the stick pad.) It has a hole, so you don't HAVE to stick it to anything permanently.

- Can add other users (beforehand, of course!)

- It works. The battery is only supposed to last about a year, though (we'll see!)

Cons:

- Bulkier than I thought - not quite as thick as a pen, but almost. About a half-dollar size.

- The FIND process takes a minute or two to adjust and is a little confusing at first.

- The FIND radius sure isn't perfectly accurate. But hey, it's something!

- Battery not replaceable. The Tile people will recycle it for you for a fee, but I doubt that is a rapid process.

I really like it. I don't lose stuff that often, but this is an awfully convenient tracking option - having a general idea is a LOT better than having NO idea at all! And I LOVE the idea of the Tile community! The Tile gives me peace of mind taking things through airports etc. If there's something you think you MIGHT mislay, I think the Tile is worth it.
text_fidelity_b: Tile - (Gen 1) - 1 Pack - Discontinued by Manufacturer

AmazonBasics Vehicle Power Cable with Mini-USB Connector for GPS and Other Mini-USB Devices This cord is marketed as a direct replacement to the Garmin power cord. That's why I purchased it. And though it features the compact right angle mini USB plug on one end and provides adequate power to run my 2505LMT, when I plug the cord into the Garmin it immediately reports that the traffic function will not work.

Upon closer examination of the OEM power coed, I observe that it has a blivet on the cord near the 12v plug end that must be the traffic receiver.

This cord has no such receiver and cannot help the 2595LMT receive traffic information.

On the other hand, most of the time traffic information is bogus. And more annoying than useful. The Garmin is constantly binging at me to take an alternate route that never is a better route.

Today I tried following its suggestion to get off the freeway in LA because the Garmin was concerned that the freeway was clogged. It told me to take La Cienega to save 4 minutes. Ha. La Cienega was much, much worse than the freeway and ended up costing me 15 minutes or more. (I think it assumes no one is using surface streets in LA in morning rush hour traffic--a fatal assumption.

Later in the trip it told me the freeway was closed ahead and to take an alternate route. I didn't believe it as I could see with my eyes and the excellent traffic flow in both directions that there was no actual blockage.

So, if you don't mind not having the traffic function, this cord works fine. (And since I don't trust the traffic function, I'll probably turn it off my self -- regardless of cord used.)

Blink XT2 Outdoor/Indoor Smart Security Camera with cloud storage included, 2-way audio, 2-year battery life – 2 camera kit This was a real disappointment. One of the main problems is that it is only compatible with 2G and if you have a 2G and a 5G network it still may not work if your network is merged and/or you have intermittent 2G. Not sure if this applies to you? It probably does if you live in the United States in a major city. Secondly the support was terrible. Have you ever call a support line and it took 20 minutes just for them to get your name your email and whatever other information they claimed they need to identify its you? Well that's exactly the type of support you can expect from Blink. They take forever and I'm not exaggerating, forever to even get to your question which they probably won't answer because they are too busy reading from their script while they ignore your questions. Don't waste your time, your money or your very sanity. Take a hard pass on this.

Update 6/10/20:
Received an email from Alex with Amazon Executive Support. Apparently the information that we received regarding our 2g/5g internet was not valid. However using an extension cord a long one we positioned the sync module closer to our wifi modem and were finally able to set up the camera. And did get it online. However, that was all.

First of all the 2 year battery life that the description touts is just plain misleading. Apparently this camera will provide that type of battery life if you only arm the camera when you are not at home and have the settings on the lowest functionality, e.g. lowest video quality, lowest sensitivity, shortest video length etc.

Even on the highest settings we the camera just does not "CONSISTENTLY" capture video of motion or people period. Comparing this camera to our blink door bell we are getting about 10% or less video capture of motion/people. However, it does capture video when there is no apparent motion and/people in the activity zones. Also some videos are for 3 seconds or less for who knows what reason.

Not sure why Blink would think that anyone would be happy with this camera and not sure what type of situation this camera would work in since it does not do what it says it does.

This camera is a mystery and is not user friendly. Support is a joke. We have spent so much time trying to figure this camera out it is ridiculous. The Ring camera door bell is much much much easier and 100 times more reliable. We are definitely sending this back.

Canon 2562A002 EF 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 is USM Standard Zoom Lens for Canon SLR Cameras The Canon 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 lens with Image Stabilization is a very capable, and more importantly, affordable lens,and is perfect for times when you just want to have one lens on the camera but you also want to have a lot of options with your focal range. While you get the benefits of a slight wide to telephoto range in one handy package, you do lose in light stops as you move through the focal range (the maximum aperture stops down as you move toward the telephoto end of the range). This is where the image stabilization comes in very handy, and allows you to keep hand shake at bay even when you have to compromise on shutter speed to get the correct exposure.

I've had no complaints about the optical quality, I think you'll be pleased with the shots you get from it - the lens may be cheap but don't confuse that with what the quality of image this lens can provide. Keep in mind on a camera with a cropped sensor (any Canon DSLR model other than the 5D and 1D models) the focal range is equivalent to @45-215mm - you lose a bit of the wide angle advantage, but you get more telephoto, so it depends which end of the focal range you value the most as to whether that is a disadvantage or not.
text_fidelity_b: Canon 2562A002 EF 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 is USM Standard Zoom Lens for Canon SLR Cameras

Logitech Cooling Pad N200 with USB-Powered 2-Speed Fan The Logitech Cooling Pad N200 is a simple padded platform your laptop rests on to keep the hot underside of the laptop from roasting your legs. It connects to the laptop with a USB plug, and draws power from the laptop to run a 2-speed cooling fan (controlled by a switch located on the USB plug).

The pad works splendidly. The fan makes only minor noise in operation even at the highest speed (no more noise than the laptop's own fans make when they engage), and I am completely protected from the heat from the underside of the laptop. The bottom of the pad is nicely padded and is comfortable in use. I didn't have to adjust my position at any point, as I often have to do with the laptop alone, when I need to shift the underside's "hot spot" to another area of my legs.

I can't speak to how much this drains the laptop battery since I very rarely use my laptop without having it plugged in via an AC adapter (my laptop battery is failing and can't run for long without being plugged into the wall).

If I had one nitpick, I would suggest to Logitech that future models have some sort of attachment feature that would allow the laptop to be securely attached to the pad. At present the laptop just rests on top of pad, with the USB connector serving as the only connection between the laptop and the pad. I'd like them to be more securely attached to one another so it's less cumbersome to carry the laptop to another room. But that is a minor issue, and I am otherwise very pleased with this.

Highly recommend!
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Cooling Pad N200 with USB-Powered 2-Speed Fan

text_fidelity_a:
D-Link Pan & Tilt Wi-Fi Camera (DCS-5009L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This camera is yet another product made in China and sold here in the United States for prices equivalent to what we'd pay if the thing was actually made in the USA, which IT IS NOT. The plastic it's made with seems cheap and brittle.

The setup instructions are WRONG and can lead you through a lengthy hell to install and configure the camera. The camera DID NOT HAVE THE MOST CURRENT SOFTWARE and I was forced through an update TWICE because the first one was the wrong one. Yes, the wrong one was recommended on their website. It took a second pass to get the correct version. Speaking of their website, it's a real mess, difficult to navigate, impossible to locate what you need on it, and just plain annoying. Tech support is mostly via email and the one time I did get a human, he didn't know much about anything.

You may want to use the camera's web interface to set up security and so forth. The GOTCHA is the cameras use Java and Java is going to drive your internet security software, firewall and virus protection wild. Java is known to be a welcome mat announcing your computer is open for all manner of malware, virus infections and so on. My security software blocked the install entirely.

Access to the camera remotely is via the D-Link website through an account you set up. To see the camera's video you must go to the website, log in and then view the camera. As video goes from camera to the D-Link website and then to you via your mobile device, the panning and zooming is jerky due to the lag in the up and download of the signal.

If you're looking for a security camera to use while traveling, or out for an evening, this will take care of things--barely. If you want a home security system with multiple cameras, go for a dedicated system with hard-wired cameras, a DVR and a solid wall around it for security. This camera is a toy compared to industrial or home-grade security.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Pan & Tilt Wi-Fi Camera (DCS-5009L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

The range on this lens takes you from a decent wide angle perspective to a mid-range telephoto without any light loss (the maximum aperture is constant throughout the zoom range) and image stabilization keeps focus problems due to hand shake well away.

Optical quality is excellent, as you would expect with an L lens, and autofocus is smooth and fast. Keep in mind on a camera with a cropped sensor (any Canon DSLR model other than the 5D and 1D models) the focal range is equivalent to @40-170mm - you lose a bit of the wide angle advantage, but you get more telephoto, so it depends which end of the focal range you value the most as to whether that is a disadvantage or not.

Tram 1185 Amateur Dual-Band Magnet Antenna I bought this Mag-Mount antenna initially for my Boafeng UV-5R+ radio after I bought a SMA-to-SO239/PL259 Connector and I was hitting repeaters over 25 miles away at 5 watts. Later I bought myself a Kenwood TM-281A mobile unit for my car an for the moment it is in use there until I figure out what kind for permanent (drill-in) antenna I want to get for my car. Problem is, this Mag-Mount antenna works so good I am debating on if I really need to get a permanent. Now there are compromises to Mag-Mounts, like cable may not be too long, etc. Eventually I will get a drill-in antenna.

For the TM-281A I have two TX power settings, 65 and 25 watts. This antenna works on both but I couldn't find any documentation on the max power for this antenna so I normally just keep it a 25 watts and it still gets out there just fine.

I would caution to tape around the area where the cable connects to the Mag-Mount to keep moisture out. I haven't have problems yet but I hear that it can be a problem for just about any mag-mounts.

For this price, buy it, test it and if you don't need it, then keep it as a backup.

73'
K9RUM

Amazon Basics Over-Ear Bluetooth Wireless Headset with Micro-USB and 3.5 Audio Cable - Black These over the ear Bluetooth earphones are just over the ear Bluetooth ear phones. They are not noise cancelling, so if that is what you want then you'd better pass on by. These are a basic Bluetooth Wireless Headphones.

Unboxing you get the headphones, and two different cords. One cord to charge the headphones (USB plug) and one cord to use the headphones outside of Bluetooth mode. I plugged them in my laptop overnight to charge it up and then took them to work to see how they would do. At work, I found out they do not cancel noise. I could still hear every single conversation around me whether music was playing or not. To drown out conversation, I would have to turn the sound way up, but I'd rather save my hearing. However, my purposes it's ok. I really just wanted the overhead head phones to indicate to people that I'm working. For some reason, earbuds just don't communicate that I'm busy. I had to use the audio cord in my mp3 (from a famous manufacturer) because I have a first generation unit that doesn't have Bluetooth ability. I felt that earbuds vs. these were no different. I decided to start with something bass inducing, so started with early 00's Hip Hop. The bass on my earbuds is better. I then worked my thru my R&B & Alternative lists, and then finally something with high pitched tones (strings) like Irish Folk. I felt that my earbuds had slightly better sound quality. However, I did not feel like was missing out on much.

Next, I brought them home and tested them out with my laptop in Bluetooth mode. Set-up was easy. My laptop has a Bluetooth icon and I just asked it to look for Bluetooth devices. After a few seconds, AmazonBasics Bluetooth Headphones popped-up. I told it to connect and then pumped up the jamz (it's always with a z). After a couple hours, I got up to adjust the thermostat on the A/C. I walked from the dining room thru the living room and into the foyer. I realized as I was walking back I still had the headphones on! I completely forgot! So, that means they are comfortable. A little heavy, but I obviously got used to it.

Finally, I tested them with my tablet (again a well-known brand) and I was not able to connect to it. I then tried to reconnect to my laptop and the laptop did not reconnect. The instructions are no good in troubleshooting this issue. So, now I have to connect via the cable all the time, which defeats the purpose. I can use the earbuds that I've been using. Plus, my laptop stopped producing sound altogether. Additionally, when they are playing everyone can hear what you listening to, so they will not be that helpful. If my son is standing next to me or sitting at the table with me, he can hear every word from my HipHop mix. Not ideal. Speaking of HipHop, another downside is that these, unlike a well-known brand with the name of a rapper/producer attached to them, do not fold up. So, they are big and bulky in your bag when you are carrying them around. I'm also afraid that something in my purse or mini backpack is going to do something to them. I also have to make sure I'm carrying a big purse to transport these around.

Pros:
-Wireless! (Don't disconnect from the device once you get it connected you'll never get it back.)
-Comfortable on the ears
-Easy set-up

Cons:
-Not Noise Cancelling
-Sound Quality could be better
-Heavy
-Does not fold up (Bulky to carry around)
-Must use the cable if you disconnect from a device. It will not reconnect.

UPDATE: The fix to my connection issue was on Pg. 6 of the instructions, but that's not how I connected the first time. Now, that I am reconnected to my laptop, the sound is like being underwater and goes in and out. So, it's tricky and sometimes you will have a set of wireless headphones, and sometimes you won't.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Over-Ear Bluetooth Wireless Headset with Micro-USB and 3.5 Audio Cable - Black

One For All Streamer Remote – Universal Remote Control for up to 3 Devices Infrared Controlled Streamer Boxes TVs and Sound bar – Learning Feature - Backlit Keys - Black – URC7935 I have an LG TV and an ancient Roku 3 purchased in 2015. I’m sick of needed multiple remotes to adjust volume and play media. I also don’t like trying to play guess the button with the Roku remote in the dark.

I ordered this up and got a brief scare when I opened it when it said not for Roku sticks. Only for Roku TVs. What??? Got back on Amazon and looked up compatibility and Roku 3’s are definitely listed as compatible. Is it considered a stick?? Not sure but it’s definitely not a Roku TV.

Anyhow. Setup was pretty easy. It actually came pre programmed to work with my Roku. That took a second to figure out. Programming for the TV only took a few minutes to follow pretty straight forward instructions.

Backlit keys are really nice. I would have put up with the standard mushy silicone keys with the weird over bright green (or blue or red) led shining around the edges.

Instead this had a nice, very subtle light that illuminates the symbol in the middle of the key.

Only con: backlight doesn’t turn on until you actually press a key. It would be more helpful if there was a “turn on the backlight” key that was somehow very distinct feeling. Then once the buttons were lit, I could select the right one.

Hopefully they will do this in their next iteration of this remote. It’s near perfect otherwise.

Edited to add:

After a few days its streamer box functions all stopped working. Tried all the different ways to program it. No dice. Checked if my original Roku remote still worked? It did. New remote still works on TV, just not on Roku. Total bummer. 🤬🤬🤬🤬🤬
text_fidelity_b: One For All Streamer Remote – Universal Remote Control for up to 3 Devices Infrared Controlled Streamer Boxes TVs and Sound bar – Learning Feature - Backlit Keys - Black – URC7935

ProElife Ultra Thin Silicone Full Size Keyboard Cover Skin for 2017 2018 Apple iMac Magic Keyboard with Numeric Keypad MQ052LL/A A1843 US Layout (Item Folded in Packaging) (Ombre Blue) UPDATE (12/25/2021):

I have removed this skin (bought on January 27, 2020) for 3 reasons.
1. The keys were not so visible below the skin because it has become more translucent instead of remaining transparent.
2. The shift key on the left side was ripped from being used and from my fingernail, I would think. IOW, it's not so tough.
3. A sticky liquid has formed between my keyboard and the skin. I removed it with more than just wiping. No solvent has been used at any time. Perhaps the silicone reacted with the plastic keys. Nothing has ever been spilled on the keyboard. Still, I have a skin on the keyboard as protection against any liquid OR dust OR hair getting into my keyboard that I have been using since 2008 when it was new.

My replacement (Allinside) is now in place and I can once again see the keys.
The skin fits the keys such that it does NOT have to wrap around the edges of the keyboard.

UPDATE (7/14/2018): After one year I have to replace this keyboard skin because it is wearing out in several places, mainly the left side command key where there is a ¼ inch slit. When I have to type a long document / letter, I remove the skin so I can type faster on the aluminum keyboard because the keys require only a light touch. I have not switched to a BT keyboard because this one is so good, and the fact that it is wired is not a problem with a little tape to keep the cable out of the way when I slide the keyboard shelf in and out. The skin I received is transparent with nothing printed on any of the keys.

For those who have the wired Apple aluminum extended keyboard (with keypad), this product fits correctly to protect the keyboard from dust and spills. It is in use on my Mac Pro (early 2008). The description says for iMac, but it fits any of these keyboards of this style, not just the iMac keyboard.

It arrives folded, but that does not matter if it comes from a seller in the US who delivers it in a timely manner.

The keyboard cover does make it necessary to slow down the typing speed. That's not a real problem unless one is a touch typist or writer who spends a lot of time on the keyboard.
text_fidelity_b: ProElife Ultra Thin Silicone Full Size Keyboard Cover Skin for 2017 2018 Apple iMac Magic Keyboard with Numeric Keypad MQ052LL/A A1843 US Layout (Item Folded in Packaging) (Ombre Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory I'm normally an ear bud user since I've never been able to find an over the ear headset that was comfortable to wear for more than 10 minutes or so at a time. Well, I found one - these are undoubtable the most comfortable headphones I've ever used. Just a dream to wear even for extended periods of time. Light, cushy, just right. And they look so elegant - a nice change from the sparse industrial look that electronics often have.

Construction quality seems very good, especially the cord (a common point of failure for me with any type of earphones). It comes with the regular and mini size plugs.

The sound quality is absolutly top-notch. I'm not an audiophile, so I can't throw out the phrases and jargon I typically read in audio discussion boards and magazines (well, I can throw them out, but not with any semblance of knowing what I'm taking about). So suffice it to say that I can't imagine anyone not being very pleased with the quality of sound using these and a MP3 player or an iPad (the two devices I've used with them so far). I've been absolutely amazed at how great these sound.

My only complaint is the lack of sound isolation. Outside sounds can easily be heard. Sometimes that's good, but most of the time I prefer to be isolated from whatever else is playing in the house. I'm finding I reach for these more often when I'm in a quiet environment, and use ear buds when there's a lot of noise about (with me defining noise as any type of music I don't care for).

With the caveat of the lack of sound blocking, these should absolutely be on your short list if you're looking for a comfortable, great sounding pair of earphones.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory

text_fidelity_a:
Fixcracked for iPad mini & iPad mini 2 9.7 inch Touch Screen Replacement Parts Digitizer Glass Assembly+ Professional Tool Kit (black) The gist: the kit is about 85% complete, the glass is easy to install, and it all works well.

I'd almost give this kit 5 stars except for a few salient omissions: the lack of instructions, and a couple of parts which I think should have been included.

There are no instructions included in the kit, and the ones in this listing are garbage. Look to other sources for how to replace the digitizer.

Everything that is included is of adequate quality, and everything was useful. I needed to provide a heat gun and safety glasses (do wear safety glasses, prescription glasses would work just as well, or a face shield--i had little pieces of glass pinging me in the face as I removed the very cracked digitizer).

All told the replacement took me 3 hours to complete. I followed instructions on the iFixit site; there were a few discrepancies but fairly trivial ones, and it included many tips, cautions, and comments, in addition to the directions, that were more than adequate to make the repair fairly easy. As I mentioned, the glass was a mess of cracks, I covered the screen with a couple of layers of packaging tape to hold the majority of shards together as I worked. Once the glass was off everything went pretty smoothly.

The two things which I think should have been included are adhesive and gloves. The glass is taped down, and at least in my case, the tape is almost impossible to recover. The gloves would make keeping the screen and glass free of finger prints. Both would be pretty cheap.
text_fidelity_b: Fixcracked for iPad mini & iPad mini 2 9.7 inch Touch Screen Replacement Parts Digitizer Glass Assembly+ Professional Tool Kit (black)

text_fidelity_a:
Jabra Evolve 40 MS Professional Wired Headset, Mono – Telephone Headset for Greater Productivity, Superior Sound for Calls and Music, 3.5mm Jack/USB Connection, All-Day Comfort Design, MS Optimized I felt the need to review because there were wildly varing reviews out there and I almost didn't purchase these. I own 3 varieties of BOSE headphones, and I needed to get a new headset with a USB connection since my work laptop is broken in that I can hear web calls but not speak. I'll address some conflicting reviews that I found to be bunk:
Comfort - I'm usually not a fan of on-ear headsets but these are padded and comfy. They aren't too light as to slip off, nor are they heavy or bulky. One reviewer said the cord and control circle (volume and mute) was so heavy as to drag the headphones off his head ... totally untrue. The cord is very long - you can slide over to your file cabinet or printer - yay. And the cord is NOT heavy as to feel its weight on that side of the headset.
Sound - The sound is excellent and as I mentioned, I'm a BOSE girl. There are so many USB headsets in the $39 - $79 range and I'm glad I spent the extra dollars for this price point. Working from home in the COVID age means a lot more WebEx and Zoom meetings, and sound - and noise cancellation - has to be excellent. One reviewer said she could hear herself breathing. That only happens when the mouthpiece is aimed at your nostril - duh. Move it.

I can't comment on longevity as these are new, but hopefully these will have a nice long usage life.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra Evolve 40 MS Professional Wired Headset, Mono – Telephone Headset for Greater Productivity, Superior Sound for Calls and Music, 3.5mm Jack/USB Connection, All-Day Comfort Design, MS Optimized

Noise cancelling – Jabra is the first headphone experience every bit the equal with the Bose 35. Other noise reduction players competing in the price bracket don’t come close. The Jabra and Bose cancellation are different. Audible net cancellation is so close to the same that I can’t discriminate. If you know what I mean, you will notice it.

Bass – Jabra by a hair

Treble – Jabra wins

Clarity – Bose by a hair

Comfort – High personal importance for air travel. Bose passes the 8-hour flight test. I believe the Jabra will too.

The Jabra 85h is incredibly impressive. It’s a competitive break-through from my perspective. The same price range as Bose 35. Overall the same with very subtle differences that make a winner impossible to my ear. I’d need an acoustics lab to compare the 2 in detail and that degree of detail would be irrelevant for me or the typical user in the price bracket.
Nobody’s going to go wrong with the Jabra 85h. Bose has the first genuine competitor in the price range. That’s good for everybody.

ZHIWHIS Shortwave Radio, MP3 Player with Weather Radios Portable AM FM, Retro Bluetooth Speaker with 6 EQ Modes, Rechargeable Alarm Clock Receiver with Sleep Time and NOAA Alerts ZWS-701 I now own two emergency types of radios, this one, and another. This means I can compare this to something directly. The following are the reasons why I like this radio more than the other:

1). It’s TINY. It can fit in the front pocket of your shirt or jacket.

2). It’s analogue. This old fashioned tuning style happens to be my preference for radios. It is simple, and you have more control in tuning into the exact radio station that you want without hassle.

3). This radio comes equipped with an antenna extension that includes what appears to be a copper coil. So if you can’t get good reception with this radio’s built in antenna, out comes this Tesla-esque looking attachment!

4). It is yellow jacket yellow. It won’t get so easily lost in the clutter, if you choose not to use it unless hazardous weather conditions are reported.

Now: things that I like less about this radio:

1). It isn’t water resistant/ waterproof

2). For the money, I think that an extra feature or two could be added. For the same price, I also have an emergency radio that has solar panels, reading lamp, compass, an SOS alarm, flashlight, a hand crank, and provides a powered docking station for my devices in case of a power outage.

But to each their own. Perhaps those reading this review aren’t interested in owning an emergency radio that is a transformer. Maybe you want to keep things simple, and are not as enamored of gadgets as I. Regardless of which radio you ultimately go with, and this one is great for size and analogue tuning, you should always keep it charged up and use it frequently enough during non emergency times that you will fully understand how it functions and not be taken by surprise by a random power outage.
text_fidelity_b: ZHIWHIS Shortwave Radio, MP3 Player with Weather Radios Portable AM FM, Retro Bluetooth Speaker with 6 EQ Modes, Rechargeable Alarm Clock Receiver with Sleep Time and NOAA Alerts ZWS-701

text_fidelity_a:
Cisco-Linksys WRT160N Wireless-N Broadband Router I was having terrible problems connecting to work from home over VPN. My MS communicator (IM) and Outlook just wouldn't work right over VPN. The help desk at work blamed by bandwidth and ISP (comcast). This didn't make sense since everyone nearly else at work also uses comcast and has the same bandwidth.

Many folks at work were also having issues with IM and said switching to a Linksys router fixed their isses - so I took the plunge. It did fix my IM. And, the wireless signal strength is better than before.

But, it didn't fix Outlook. Linksys and my IT help folks looked at it. I spent more time rebooting my computer in the past week than I could stand.

Outlook still would not work over my wireless but I could connect with no issues over my neighbors unsecured network. I called Comcast and they wanted to upgrade my modem's software but said the thing was soooo old it had to be replaced. A comcast guy was at my house by later in the day and replaced my modem in less than one hour - half of that on-hold waiting for the tech guy at comcast proper to pick up the phone so they could work together.

Within minutes of the modem being set up I was happily working away over VPN using Outlook and IM and everything else. It's nearly as fast as being in the office. My connection over VPN and not over VPN is clearly faster than before - it's also less prone to drop outs.

Long story short. It's a great router but don't expect it to fix everything. Make sure your modem is the most up to date both in terms of hardware and software too. Basically, any piece of anything between you and your internet could gum up the works and it's hard knowing where the issues is (router, modem, network card, etc.) I can't believe the number of well trained tech people I spoke to and not one of them questioned the modem. All of them seemed to think since I could get to the internet not over VPN that using VPN should make no difference. Clearly it did - apparently older modems don't play well with VPN.
text_fidelity_b: Cisco-Linksys WRT160N Wireless-N Broadband Router

It had been causing the indoor alarm unit to sound without ceasing. I removed the batteries to see what might be the problem, and I found ANTS had taken up residency inside the sensor unit. After clearing as many ants as possible, I put the unit in a plastic bag that is sealed. It will be several days before I open the unit to clean the circuit board as well as the housing. Then I will attempt to seal all openings so that I can use the sensor. It may not operate reliably once all the openings are sealed, but I have no other choice.

The second sensor is not giving me any problem because it is in a location that ants will not frequent.

As for locating the sensor in my mailbox so I will know when someone has opened the mailbox door, that won't work. The metal mailbox prevents a signal from being transmitted the 100 feet to the alarm. Also, ants like to use the mailbox which makes me spray an insecticide when I see them, and that's usually once a year.
text_fidelity_b: Driveway Alarm Wireless Outside, 1byone Motion Sensor Alarm 1000 FT Range Extra Loud Chimes Home Security Alarm System with 1 Receiver 2 Weatherproof Infrared Sensors Protect Indoor/Outdoor Property

I'VE BOUGHT 3 FOR GRANDDAUGHTER'S USE WHEN THEY COME TO VISIT, AND NOT A SINGLE ONE LASTED MORE THAN A FEW MONTHS) for even a third of the price. Just don't expect the same experience you may be used to on your Android smartphone or tablets that you now have.

text_fidelity_a:
XBOOM Mini Portable Capsule Speaker with Rechargeable Battery and Enhanced Bass+ Resonator (Mini - Black) -1 pack I've been using an Altec Lansing iM227 (a model that is no longer produced by Altec Lansing, but comparable models are still offered) for a couple of years and have been very pleased with it. The Xboom, however, gives me much the same performance at half the size.

The sound quality of the Xboom is impressive for the size. It puts out nearly the same bass level as the iM227, which is surprising given how small it is. It does suffer a bit in the mid and upper ranges, which do not come through as clearly and sharply as the iM227. But the output is more than adequate for enjoyment.

I really like how the two halves of the speaker can be closed up and turned into a small ball that is only about 2 inches tall. Very compact so it easily fits into a bag or jacket pocket - this speaker is designed to be carried around easily. It comes with a decent cloth pouch plus a USB charge cable.

While it will work when it is in its compact mode, for best sound it needs to be unlatched so it expands to about 3 inches tall.

Unlike the iM227 it has an internal battery (the iM227 runs on 3 AAA batteries). That's both good and bad: good for ease of use and compact size; bad in case the internal battery fails, which renders the speaker useless. The Xboom has a stated run time of "up to 12 hours" according to the specs, which is pretty accurate - I got about 10 hours out of a fresh battery. Recharge time is about 2 hours.

Operation is very simple: plug in the attached cable to your device (I'm using it as a speaker for a small mp3 player), turn it on, and listen. The Xboom has a volume control, which the iM227 lacks, and an on/off switch. There's a power indicator light on the bottom of the speaker.

Unlike the iM227, the Xboom can be daisy-chained to other Xbooms for a bigger sound. I only have one, so I can't say how well that works, but it's a nice feature.

Complaints are virtually nil. If I had to come up with something, I'd say that it would be nice to have the power indicator light on the top rather than the bottom so it would be more easily visible as a reminder to power down and save battery life. Minor point, however.

While the sound quality of the Altec Lansing is better, the size and convenience of the Xboom makes it the one I'll take along with me and use more often. Very good value for the price, and I would highly recommend it.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: XBOOM Mini Portable Capsule Speaker with Rechargeable Battery and Enhanced Bass+ Resonator (Mini - Black) -1 pack

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR 8-Port Ultra60 PoE Multi-Gigabit Ethernet Plus Switch (MS108EUP) - Managed, with 4 x PoE++ and 4 x PoE+ @ 230W, Desktop or Wall Mount, and Limited Lifetime Protection I received this item through the Amazon Vine program, although the usual green writing may not be shown. The review is specifically for model: GS305EPP.

Port Binding: I noticed that the Netgear chart shows for the "plus" series of switches, that only models with 16 or more ports support port binding. However, through the web interface, I was able to do a single instance of port binding (it looks like it allows you to bind up to four ports, although I can't think of an instance where binding more than two ports on a five port switch would be worthwhile). I learned some quirks about port binding in the process, that using 802.3ad with multiple Linux servers doesn't allow for more than a Gb of data in any one direction anyway. BUT this switch does apparently support balance-rr, because I could get almost 2Gb/s over a 2Gb aggregate link. I think my hard drives in those machines were maxed out at that point. As I understand it, balance-rr has a high error rate because it uses striping and not all machines support it. But it was working quite nicely with my NAS units and this switch (I was expecting the 8 port switch, which would have made that setup more worthwhile because I could fatten the links on all three servers.

Although my current Netgear Pro AP does not have two ports for binding, I did have an AP before that supported it, in which case that feature on this switch may be an excellent option (particularly considering it is PoE). I haven't done the math for myself, but I think that port binding is almost a gimmick on APs because there is so much overhead on WiFi that even if your AP has a throughput in the multi-Gb range, enough of that is overhead created by the AP that you're not actually getting that much data from one computer to another.

Insight and Web Interface: The Insight App shows this switch (and my Netgear APs) as having "limited support" (just shows basic device info and a link to the device's webpage), so they're not really trying to get users of the "plus" line to subscribe to that in perpetuity.

And you don't need the app to use the switch. You don't even need the configuration page, really: I just plugged this into my old 24-port unmanaged Netgear workhose and it picked up an IP from the router and worked just like an unmanaged switch until I decided to give it a static IP and manage it.

I was really surprised how many features are packed into the management software, considering these are Netgear's lower line of managed devices. But most of the stuff you'll see on huge enterprise devices is here as well (well, it's been a while since I've been inside the big enterprise stuff, but all those goodies reach us as consumers before long).

The web interface is just like any other network device - you can reach it from any webpage and it is super GUI - probably just a little more than I really want it to be, but it is very intuitive and you can find everything with a few clicks. I say "super GUI" just because it looks fancier than I need it to. And one thing I find a little irritating is that when you expand one box, it collapses another, so you can't look at everything at once. This doesn't really matter, but I'm old school where I just want substance over style and even style that doesn't sacrifice substance still looks like they're trying too hard.

PoE: Clearly, on this 4+1 port switch, all four of your devices can use a full 30w each, so this is non-blocking in PoE+ as well as throughput. At time of writing, the 8 port with the same power budget was actually cheaper, so you might consider that, even if you can't use all the ports at full PoE.

What is great about this, is that besides just being able to add APs and IP cameras to your network (or even lighting, etc.), you can turn them on and off from the web interface. So I can keep my main AP on PoE (and therefore on my telecom closet's backup power supply), and then turn my detached garage's AP on and off from the web interface rather than having to go down to the basement and plug or unplug the PoE injector every time I want to use the garage AP (I just turn it on if I'm going to be working out there and might need to watch some "how-to" videos or control my audio system from the local LAN).

*Netgear, if you're listening, I would love to have a super lightweight (and free) app that works remotely (when not necessarily on LAN) to turn ports on and off for exactly this type of reason.*

Construction: Solid device, very dense and professional looking. Plenty of lights that tell you a lot from a glance. Power supply is external and about as big as the device itself. Would personally love a way to rack mount this AND the power supply (for maximum flexibility) in 1 RU, but of course I realize most people don't want to waste a whole rack unit on 5 ports. But for the space both pieces take up, it's about a mid size unit that could be mounted with "wings". It does have four-way keyhole mounts for wall-mounting.

Background: I have great experience with Netgear for my home (but way better than most homes') network. I'd definitely use all their devices were I doing work for small or medium sized businesses. I like them just a tad less when they start trying to sell you subscriptions (which is what I hate about Brocade and Cisco, along with all the proprietary garbage), but for the most part, Netgear is inexpensive and quite reliable. I've had a 24 port nonblocking unmanaged Gb switch running 24/7 in my dusty basement for over 15 years without a single fault AND they still sell that model. Their APs are the best I've had, and I don't think I've ever had a Netgear item break on me, period. I have had lots of other home/SMB stuff break or otherwise have strange issues, though.

That said, there's a lot of no-name PoE switches on the market right now. I don't need any of those handling my low voltage needs OR my data. And they won't beat this line on the price by too much anyway.

This is an excellent device which adds a lot of versatility to your network.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR 8-Port Ultra60 PoE Multi-Gigabit Ethernet Plus Switch (MS108EUP) - Managed, with 4 x PoE++ and 4 x PoE+ @ 230W, Desktop or Wall Mount, and Limited Lifetime Protection

text_fidelity_a:
10 Inch Tablet, 64GB Storage Tablets, Android 11 Tab, 512GB Expandable, 8MP+2MP Camera, 1.5Ghz CPU Quad-Core Processor, 2GB RAM WiFi 6000mAh Battery, 10.1'' HD 1280*800 IPS Touch Screen Google Tablet I was one of the FIRST people to own an iPad back when they were introduced. It was a birthday gift. And, I honestly regret giving up a trip to Disneyland for it. Yes, I had a choice between what I thought was going to be a lifelong, productive item for a trip to Disneyland.

I did go to Disneyland in 2015 though, so I was a few years late. Regrets? Should’ve taken the trip and NOT gotten the iPad. It barely works today (can’t upgrade the iOS due to NOT having a camera – a front facing one for some updates). And, I have it in my desk drawer. REALLY PEEVED at Apple for that one.

So, I’ve been REAL hesitant to jump on the eReader or tablet train. They upgrade, change, and modify so fast. Honestly, I use my iPhone for certain things while I use my laptop. The rest? I use my laptop. I don’t really read eBooks to justify an eReader, nor do I like it. [I did try it with this – still a no go – clunky, awkward, no “book smell”, and so easy to lose my place.]

Seeing this? I decided to grab it. After all, I USED to be a Samsung Galaxy (Android) user. I had to replace my GS8 and the iPhone I was had a cheaper plan through my carrier. No regrets there. But, I still remember the Android system. My mom still has her GS8 phone, so I HAVE to know it.

Looking at the price, around $60 (as of this review) – this is a basic, no frills tablet. It is a “no-name” brand, but that doesn’t mean much. I’ve had trouble with numerous brand name items, so name doesn’t matter.

Now, this is VERY SLOW. Even a cheap Acer laptop can be slow. My mom had one and the language … hello? Content warning!!

This is, to me, great for pre-teens and teens. It’s not too expensive that parents will really scream if something happens (like say an iPad or more expensive $100+ tablet). Or, it can work for someone who wants some internet functionality, and wants to read eBooks. The Kindle app works great here, just not my style.

I can check my email accounts – Outlook and Gmail – no real issues. I’ve ordered fast-food. As far as games? The one I tried didn’t work (Hogwarts Mystery)

As far as a user manual – like most devices nowadays (or the ones I’ve bought in the last 5-8 years) – the MANUAL (instructions) are on the device, usually a PDF. This was the same for the last three HP laptops I bought in 2010, 2011, and 2019. And, it was the same for the last two phones (GS8 and iPhone 11). Also, my iPods in 2008 and 2013. So, yes, I do have a LOT of experience with the lack of a physical manual. The manual can be accessed by swiping the homescreen UP. It is a PDF file.

There are some apps that ARE NOT COMPATIBLE with this device, even if you have them on a Galaxy phone. These can range from productivity to fast food. IE: Tropical Smoothie Café’s app is compatible, Taco Bell isn’t. My bank’s app isn’t compatible, but I can access the website through the Chrome browser (which I also have on my iPhone).

However, a GIANT bonus for me – MICROSOFT 365. I was able to add WORD to the tablet, and since I have cloud storage – ALL MY DOCUMENTS are AVAILABLE to view and edit.

Overall – this is, as I stated: a BASIC or STARTER tablet. Better suited for ages 8 to 15. I say this based on the fact that at 8, I would be able to care for this, and use it. By 15, I’d likely save up my allowance for a higher priced tablet or get it as a gift.

I am pretty pleased with it, and will likely use it for several things.
text_fidelity_b: 10 Inch Tablet, 64GB Storage Tablets, Android 11 Tab, 512GB Expandable, 8MP+2MP Camera, 1.5Ghz CPU Quad-Core Processor, 2GB RAM WiFi 6000mAh Battery, 10.1'' HD 1280*800 IPS Touch Screen Google Tablet

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech MX Master 3S for Mac Wireless Bluetooth Mouse, Ultra-Fast Scrolling, Ergo, 8K DPI, Quiet Clicks, Track on Glass, USB-C, Apple, iPad - Space Grey - With Free Adobe Creative Cloud Subscription I’m really picky when it comes to mice. I usually end up with a gaming mouse because they are comfortable and fulfill my needs. But because I use a Mac, it’s rare that I can customize buttons and macros and all that.

So I was really excited to try out the Logitech MX Master 3. I’ve been using it for the past month and keep going back to it. I have two work spaces in my house, and I find myself taking the mouse from desk to desk, instead of using what’s already on the desk.

The mouse feels nice in my hand. I have small hands (size small in gloves), and the mouse nestles nicely against my palm. My fingers don’t have to stretch to reach any of the buttons. The thumb rest is comfortable. I only wish the mouse had better pinky support.

The scroll wheel … I love the scroll wheel. Logitech calls it the “MagSpeed™ Electromagnetic” scroll wheel which is a really fancy way of saying it scrolls like butter. The wheel is nearly silent and super precise. It has just the right amount of feedback when scrolling slowly through a page, and flies when I want to get to the bottom of a long article. It really is a joy to use.

The mouse charges via USB-C and includes a USB-C to USB-C cable. I couldn’t try out the Flow option, where you can copy/paste text, images, and files between computers because my other Mac’s version of iOS is too old to install Logitech Options. But I was able to connect the mouse to both of my Macs and switch between them using the 1, 2, 3 button on the bottom.

Logitech Options offers a decent amount of customization. You can customize settings across all applications, such as pointer and scrolling speed. Some of the buttons can be customized: gesture, scroll wheel click, wheel shift, horizontal scroll, back, and forward.

App specific options can be assigned to the buttons. Defaults are assigned for the most popular programs like Chrome and Photoshop, and I was able to add customizations for my personal favorite, Scrivener.

But what I don’t like is that I’m limited in picking what the buttons can do. I really wanted to change the horizontal scroll wheel into another vertical scroll wheel, but I can’t. I can only do the functions Logitech thinks I want, such as zooming or navigating between tabs.

The MX Master 3 has a lot of nice functions and has been designed for productivity. I’ve barely touched on a lot of what you can do with this mouse.

I just wish I could customize *everything* because what I need for productivity doesn’t match what someone else needs, or what Logitech assumes I want.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech MX Master 3S for Mac Wireless Bluetooth Mouse, Ultra-Fast Scrolling, Ergo, 8K DPI, Quiet Clicks, Track on Glass, USB-C, Apple, iPad - Space Grey - With Free Adobe Creative Cloud Subscription

Belkin Grip Candy Sheer Case for iPhone 5 and 5S (Purple and Turquoise) This is the second case I have gotten that I could not give a good rating because of the bottom part, which does not fit with the adapter (to allow older devices to work with the new iPhone), and it does not fit most professional cables that go into the headphone jack.
Because my car has a built-in charger and system that plays with i-technology (previous generations), I HAVE to use the adapter, not just the new wire. Because I am a dancer and instructor and use my phone for job every day, I HAVE to have a case that lets me plug into our system. For those reasons, this case, like the last one I got, is useless to me.

Could you peel back the case to leave the bottom exposed? Yes. But over time, this warps the plastic and creates a loose fit, and putting it on and taking if off can cause the screen protector to come off around the edges.

Could you cut part of the bottom to allow the adapter and wires to fit? No. The plastic is thick enough that the wire will still not fit the headphone jack. As for the adapter, it might fit, but it will want to come out because the thickness, again, will make it want to separate.

So far, the only case to fit my iPhone is a pretty cheap import that has very thin plastic and is generally not a great case either. Is it a design problem with the phone as well? Maybe, but the people making cases should take that into account and design something that works with the iPhone 5 as it is, not as we wish it were. I guess I'm keeping my brand X case a bit longer.

text_fidelity_a:
Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100 The mouse functions fine and I do like the form of it. There is one critical problem though. The form forces the forward and back buttons to be on the opposite side of left and right click so while your thumb is on the forward or back, you have no choice but to squeeze the right or left click to engage the forward/back button. Obviously, this causes inadvertent clicks with the mouse which is a problem. It happens mainly on the forward button as this is where the left and right click start to engage, too (more forward on the mouse itself).

I have not decided if I will keep it or not as I rely heavily on the use of these buttons. If I can find a way to grip it so this does not occur, it will be fine. In the meantime, I'll be using it look for a mouse that is designed better.

UPDATE 2-23-16: Like many others who have posted less than favorable reviews, Anker customer support has reached out to me directly, twice, offering a full refund, which I declined. In my opinion, the mouse works well for it's price, but I stand by the issue noted above. I have gotten used to is and can grip the mouse slightly differently when using the forward button. For this reason and for the outstanding customer service, I have bumped the review to 3 stars and wouldn't hesitate to recommend trying it out given the extremely low risk.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100

Audio-Technica ATH-LS50iSBK In-Ear Monitor Headphones with In-Line Mic & Control, Black As a disclaimer, I'm just an ordinary consumer (vs. a technical expert) when it comes to headphones, speakers, or earbuds. Having said that, here's my experience with these in-ear headphones:

As earbuds go, these are not as lightweight as the much cheaper, AmazonBasics and Panasonic ones I have owned. However, it's a weight difference that isn't really a problem, once I get them securely fastened around my ears.

The sound is wonderful. It has much more clarity than the inexpensive earbuds I usually buy. So to some extent the adage, "You get what you pay for," seems to apply here.

These earbuds have a useful extra: they have a microphone built in. Because of that, you can use it to speak on your cellphone, if you'd rather use this than a Bluetooth. Or if you are listening to entertainment media on your cell phone when you get a call, you won't have to unplug this earbud to take the call.

The microphone control has only one button, an on/off toggle switch. There are no volume adjustment buttons.

These earbuds seem to be well constructed. The cord is thicker and sturdier than my low-cost AmazonBasics and Panasonic earbuds.

The piece that fits into your ear has a relatively large casing compared to my other earbuds, but no doubt this is because the technology is more complicated.

These earbuds are an expensive buy for those of us who normally pay $7-12 for earbuds, but if you like to listen to music, it might be worth it.

I always like my electronics to have buttons and especially my kindle since I tend to read with one thumb on the screen itself I worried that if I upgraded to this, my thumb would either end up turning pages too soon or it wouldn't be sensitive enough to read my thumb when I wanted to. My old kindle no longer took a charge after 6 years so I had to upgrade and literally the only reason I went with this over anything else (I was wanting to get another one of my old kindles) was the backlight. I have insomnia so I'm often awake in bed with my snoring boyfriend next to me so having a light on isn't an option so having a kindle with a backlight would be ideal.

Turns out my worry over not having a button was all in vain! The touch screen has just the right amount of sensitivity. It's not so sensitive that resting my thumb on the screen where it's comfortable activates anything, but it's not so dull that I can't turn the pages easily. The back lighting is adjustable so I don't have to blind myself and I don't have to use it if I don't want to if I've got plenty of natural light. The screen is clear and crisp, it fits comfortably in my hand and the amount of books I can fit on there is insane! I've currently got 200 titles and I've still got plenty of room for more. It moves faster than my old kindle and the charge is amazing. I've been using it for over a month now and I'm still at 25% battery without charging it once aside from the day I received it.

This is by far the best kindle I've ever had!

text_fidelity_a:
Jawbone ICON HD - Bluetooth Headset - Black - Retail Packaging Freeway Driving seems to render most headsets useless.
THIS ONE WORKS EVEN ON A NOISY FREEWAY. I did a fair bit of research and read many professional and online reviews looking for a headset that would actually be intelligible to me and to the person I'm calling when I'm on the road. Mostly I use it on the road.

Other headsets got good reviews, and I had tried to find a good one for my iPhone 5. They were fine for indoors and walking, but on the road, voice recognition wouldn't work and I had trouble hearing even road directions from Google Maps.

THIS ONE WORKS and the sound is great. It's a cliche in headset reviews to say that the people you're talking to don't know you're on a headset and say it sounds like a regular phone. For me, this is the first headset where that has been true.

FIT: Fit is always going to be a personal thing. The inside the ear springy loop silicone earpiece works for me. Others are going to need the hook (or both).
I found it to be pretty comfortable, but...

HEAVY AND BULKY: Compared to many headsets (most), this is thick and heavy. It's very noticeably larger and heavier than other headsets I've used. It's not a big problem, but it's not discreet. (That's why they always photograph it so you can't see the thickness)..

BATTERY: I'm not a really heavy user, so I can't say much about talk time. Standby time is noticeably shorter than with other headsets I've used. I haven't measured, but I know I have to charge this significantly more often than my old headsets.

BUT IT WORKS: My old headsets were smaller, lighter, more comfortable and easier to use.
But they didn't work well when I needed them most. I'll take bigger, heavier, and whatnot but WORKS.

text_fidelity_a:
Polaroid Cube+ 1440p Mini Lifestyle Action Camera with Wi-Fi & Image Stabilization (Red) [[VIDEOID:c23012732deceb9d78b96d41ac89bfcb]] [[VIDEOID:56e6589f81a80deb1709b51fc87a42ef]] [[VIDEOID:bdf9b77251e219b84bed6372225dbf2a]] [[VIDEOID:838bfc2c03ad2a6d884b05f4a37eddbe]] [[VIDEOID:f7f3bb80516774e2cc828f076249211a]] [[VIDEOID:d48cd1a96b9a119e675001d320845a53]] [[VIDEOID:9363c8a20797fe64545aeb51179ca502]] [[VIDEOID:3371609d21e77efbab0cfd0f6265a782]] This is a terrific little action camera that has remarkable clear video, good audio and is extremely easy to use. I understand there were some problems with audio in the earlier versions, but it seems to be all fixed now because the sound quality was excellent when tested both indoors and outside.

I won't bore you with going over all of the specs which you can read in the product description, but I'll tell you how easy it is to use. Mine arrived partially charged, so I used my fingernail to open the back port and inset the included 8gb micro SD card, then charged it fully within an hour. On a full battery it can operate for about 107 minutes and when depleted it takes between 1.5 to 2 hrs to fully charge.

I downloaded the app to my iPad for free from the app store, then did some testing. It connected easily to my WiFi and the interface understandable and easy to use giving you the choice to shoot still photos or videos in several different resolutions. You can also import the photos or videos taken with the camera to your cell phone, your iPad, or share them using the WiFi connection to import them.

This little camera takes gorgeous high def photos, and the audio inside is crystal clear. When I was offered the opportunity by the manufacturer to test the Cube+ I went ahead and purchased a [[ASIN:B00NXK3JTI Polaroid Helmet Mount for the Polaroid CUBE, CUBE+ HD Action Lifestyle Camera]] so I would be able to properly test it in action in order to determine video and sound quality outside in the elements.

I attached the helmet mount to my 9 y/o granddaughter's helmet, placed the Cube+ in it, started it through the app on my iPad and sent her out on her scooter to see how the video and audio quality was. I've attached a short part of the video here so you can assess it for yourself, but I'm quite pleased with the quality of both the picture and the sound, and I didn't experience any lag time in regards to the app.

It does record video in MP4 format, so if you have trouble hearing the audio on your computer you should download QuickTime Player or VLC Player. Both downloads are free and should allow you to view the files and hear the audio. VLC also has a free converter available in case you prefer to use Windows Media Player or Windows Movie Maker. I use a free app called Trim & Cut on my iPad which shortens, condenses, and converts my videos to the format I prefer, and that's what I used for the video I've attached here.

This is a reasonably priced tough little action camera that's easy to use and produces great quality video. It's weather resistant and splashproof so it can handle the outdoors already, but I plan to buy the waterproof case for it so we can have fun swimming with it on this summer. I don't own a GoPro, so I have nothing to compare this to, but from a user's stand point I can definitely tell you that this is user friendly, easy to operate and does a remarkably good job! Enjoy!

This camera was provided at no cost by the manufacturer for evaluation and review.
text_fidelity_b: Polaroid Cube+ 1440p Mini Lifestyle Action Camera with Wi-Fi & Image Stabilization (Red)

The system doesn't work for me if I have to climb a ladder every other day to pull and charge the over-the-door camera.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: So far, so good.

I have been waiting to review this to see whether it had any of the problems my other systems have had. I have a hardwired analog system that failed when I tried to check footage of a creepy guy hanging outside my front door. The DVR kacked, and the disk has proprietary formatting. If you insert it in a new DVR, there is no way to keep it from reformatting the disk, so you can't ever recover footage once a DVR dies.

ARLO triggers too slowly and doesn't record long enough to catch most activity. Plus, it has battery life issues. Ring Doorbell works great when it works, which is sporadically at best.

So far, this has them beat. I've gotten battery life exceeding four days. And it catches most events I'd want to see. Image quality is great. The only thing so far is that the file sizes are enormous, but that's because of the image quality.

So far, I cautiously recommend this, certainly over ARLO and Ring. I will update as more becomes clear.

text_fidelity_a:
Lexar JumpDrive S73 64GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive LJDS73-64GASBNA (Green) I'm not going to bother with a detailed listing of times as many other reviewers have done a nice job with that. I'll just say that I did time out this device in comparison to a pair of my 2.0 flashdrives and another 3.0 on a pair of Macs, one with 2.0 USB and one with 3.0 USB. There's no doubt it's speedier in all cases than my 2.0s, whether I was transferring over a folder with a lot of docs or a folder with mixed media (docs, photos, video). Roughly 2-3 times as fast than 2.0 consistently (that's with both of them in the 2.0 ports), though the gap narrowed with really large, mixed folders. When it goes into the 3.0, it was consistently 3-4 times faster, with again a narrower gap with really large, mixed files. In comparison to a Triton, it was definitely significantly and noticeably slower, a little bit better than half as fast.

The device feels very light and the casing not quite as sturdy as my other drives, though I never feel like it's in danger of breaking. Just doesn't have the same sense of heft and durability.

On the other hand, the slide clicks in nicely and solid, with a satisfying sound and doesn't retract easily unless you are wanting it to

If you have a 2.0 drive, it'll be noticeably faster and if you're looking for a drive, makes sense to get one that can go with you to your next upgrade. If you've upgraded to 3.0 and want a new drive just for that, there's no doubt you'll notice the difference, and especially with large files and movies etc. I'd ay it's definitely worth it. As for going beyond to the Triton, personally my need for speed isn't that great--this one would suit me fine. Some people though have less patience than I do. Plus, I'm cheap. So slower than the other 3.0, but I'd say still a fine value.
text_fidelity_b: Lexar JumpDrive S73 64GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive LJDS73-64GASBNA (Green)

I have been trying to use Windows Backup with a drive attached via USB to this unit. I

make it work.

The router has its own settings that will operate reguardless if the computer works or not. The computer has nothing to do with the router software one way or the other. If you need to back up the router setting then I suggest you take screen shots of the router to verify that you can save the settings from there.
Thanks Aaron Asus Support Team

Well, I am still trying to figure out what their response means...

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung BD-H5900 3D Blu-Ray Disc Player (2014 Model) Packaging--very minimal, which is nice. Box was just enough to fit the machine safely and snugly--no over packaging

Set up--lightning fast. Pop two (included) batteries in the remote, attach to TV, plug in, choose a language, connect to home wi-fi and ready to go in two minutes at the most. Check for software upgrade, there is one, download--all done in another minute.

Apps: Seems to be a lot of back and forth on Amazon Prime. Mine definitely does not support. These are the apps from the newest software update (June 20th, 2014)
hulu plus,
VUDU
Youube
Netflix
Opera TV store
Flixster
CinemaNow
Rhapsody
Picasa
AccuWEather
Twitter
Pandora
Target
Internet TV--horrible interface
Flickr
Facebook

To be honest, I wouldn't use most of these, so I'm not all that impressed with the Apps, though certainly they have the most needed on one in Netflix. But as I have Amazon Prime, I'm sticking with our DVD player that allows me to access it (I also have an Apple TV, which is why these apps don't do much for me). I'll also say some of these apps had terrible interfaces (yes, I'm looking at you Internet TV)

Build quality: I don't know if it really matters at all with a DVD player--I mean, it's going to sit up there and not really get any abuse I assume. But it does feel a bit light, not all that solid. If it were something portable and had that feel, I'd have some concerns. Not so much with this kind of device. It has a relatively small footprint.

I had not problem with several DVDs, both blu-ray and regular. Menu movement was fast, start-up time no different from any others I've used--not noticeably better or worse. Picture was fine, again, no better or worse than others I've sued (Sony, JVC)

screen is a bit too bright. Personally, I'd find it annoying, but others may not notice.

It's not a bad player at all, does most of what it needs to OK, but I definitely prefer our Sony for its larger app features and dimmer screen (it also feels more sturdy).
text_fidelity_b: Samsung BD-H5900 3D Blu-Ray Disc Player (2014 Model)

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz M1 in-Ear Noise Isolating Earphones While these don’t offer the sound quality of higher-end Brainwavz buds (or higher-end models from other brands), the sound quality and overall performance is quite good for the price point, and the comfort is excellent.

The best description I can offer of the sound quality is “clean.” The upper and mid ranges come through very clearly and are far more well-defined than typical with budget/value earbuds. The bass is not pronounced. It’s there, but it’s not what I’d describe as punchy. These are not an ideal set if you’re looking for head-thumping bass.

The comfort is typical for Brainwavz, which is to say it’s excellent. There’s a variety of ear tips so you can customize the fit to your ear. I’m especially fond of the Comply foam tips since they provide a great (but still comfortable) seal. That helps maintain good sound isolation and also helps with the bass response. It also helps keep the earbuds in place while exercising.

The cords are thin but seem sturdy enough for typical use. The same for the ear buds themselves. While they don’t have as solid of a build quality as higher-priced models, I don’t get the feeling that these will be falling apart anytime soon. That being said, it would have been nice to have more reinforcement where the cord meets the earbud, since that’s a prime stress point in use (even though these come with a very well made carry case, more often than not I just wind them around whatever device I am using).

For the price these are hard to beat. Highly recommend these as a not too expensive way to substantially upgrade from the stock earbuds that come with many devices.
[Sample provided for review]

text_fidelity_a:
Pivotal Living Tracker 1 (2nd Generation) Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I came to this tracker cold. The Housemate has a Fitbit, but I never used it, and really haven't paid a lot of attention to what it did so I had no expectations of what the Pivotal Living tracker might do. However before I tell you what I discovered, let me explain some things about myself. I'm in my sixties, and have a sedentary job. I would like to be more active, I would like to compare my actual sleep habits against what I perceive them to be, I would like to keep an eye on hydration. I have some other goals, but these are the main ones that apply to my use of the tracker.

So how does the Pivotal Living tracker stand up to these goals? First off, because so much of my everyday movement is not easily measurable by the tracker, I'm not really getting an accurate step count. (Moving around the house holding things doesn't always register. Sitting and doing something like folding laundry sometimes does.) This is a bit of a problem because it makes it difficult to estimate how I'm doing on my step goal. So, accuracy in step count? Not so much. Going to stick to a pedometer or pedometer app. C, maybe C+ because I can set my own goals based on my health and how my day is going. (Right now I have a torn meniscus, and all my steps are limping or cane-assisted. Not fun, and not conducive to accurate step counts.)

Hydration? Great, unless you forget to enter an amount until after midnight. Whoops, sorry, can't add anything to your daily total. This is a huge oversight IMO. I sometimes finish my daily amount late in the evening when I'm not thinking about using the mobile app. However, the process of tracking it on your own is a good one. They simply need to fix the access problem. B+

Daily activity. Honestly I have NO clue how this is tracked. I'd have thought it was step-based, but I've never yet had daily activity show up on my dashboard, so there has to be some other way this band tracks activity. However, having an activity alarm that reminds me to stop what I'm doing, get up and walk around for a few minutes... that's immensely valuable to me. Without it, I'd simply forget and keep on writing or editing. I'm going to give it an A because I love the alarm which can be set for 20/40/or 60 minutes.

The rest? Sleep alarm... I've been wakened by this exactly once, when I was very nearly awake anyway. Every other morning it's done zip. I'll wake up an hour later and think, "Wha?" It's back to my clock radio. C, at best. However the sleep tracker seems surprisingly accurate based on what I remember of my nights. It fairly accurately charts how many times I've woken up, and how much good sleep I've gotten. I find this quite reassuring. A, even A+.

Calories burned: Since this is both step and activity based, it's pretty useless for me. Anyway, my goal isn't about calories, it's about activity, so I'm not going to grade this part of the app. Also, weight: Clearly this is another sub-app like hydration, which requires you to input your numbers. It keeps my weight in front of me which is a good thing, but it's not really something I feel I can adequately grade.

Problem: If you take it off it will turn itself off. I tried to put it on my desk when I was typing since it interfered with the position of my wrist. I could hear the activity alert when the band buzzed against the desk, but then it stopped because the tracker had shut down. I thought it was out of juice and couldn't figure out why I was getting less than 24 hours on the battery. When I finally figured it out, I had to start wearing it up high on my arm. Fortunately the band is big enough to allow it to sit several inches above my wrist.

Price: Very, very good. I recognize that the modest cost of the tracker is intended to get you to buy the yearly subscription, but I don't mind that. If the service works, I'm happy to pay $1 a month for it. That's still minor league stuff. However I get frequent errors saying that the goal information can't be updated from the site, and I get odd readings on my dashboard. However, by the end of the day it's usually sorted itself out, so I don't have a lot of quibbles so far.

Overall, and taking price into account I think I'd give this a B, at least for my needs. It reminds me of the things I need to remember to do, and it gives me a place where I can keep track of those goals. The cost to do this is, as I indicated, quite modest. If you're not ready to drop a lot of money on a more sophisticated tracker, give the Pivotal Living tracker a try.

Note: I'm using this on a Fire phone, which means I had to side-load the app. The instructions on how to install Google Play and everything else you need to side load Google Play apps are available on You Tube, and it's dead easy. Once you've done that, just go to the Play Store and download the Pivotal Living app, and have at it.
text_fidelity_b: Pivotal Living Tracker 1 (2nd Generation) Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
